chunks: And from a sermon of him (peace be upon him), which he delivered to rouse the people when the news of the campaign of Al-Anbar with the army of Muawiya arrived, but they did not rise [to fight].
In it, he mentions the virtue of jihad, rouses the people, mentions his knowledge of war, and places the blame upon them for their lack of obedience to him.

key_terms.الْأَنْبَارِ: Al-Anbar (a location in Iraq, site of a military campaign)
key_terms.الْجِهَادِ: Jihad (striving/struggle in the path of God)
key_terms.مُعَاوِيَةَ: Muawiya (the Umayyad caliph and rival of Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What was the context and purpose of Imam Ali's sermon regarding the campaign of Al-Anbar?
ai.summary: Delivered during the pivotal period of the Battle of Siffin, this sermon underscores the political and spiritual crisis of the 'People of the Book' (Ahl al-Kitab) who, despite their faith, lacked the martial zeal of the early companions. Imam Ali (AS) contrasts his own military expertise and readiness with the populace's lethargy, attributing their failure to rise not to a lack of capability, but to a deficiency in their commitment to his Imamate and the cause of justice.
